violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: containers of raw, cracked eggs were stored over fresh lettuce in the walk-in.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The PIC moved the eggs to another location to avoid this possible cross-contamination.

violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Surfaces of ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment are not being cleaned as required. The food employee stated the soda dispenser nozzles are cleaned every two weeks. The manufacturer recommends cleaning them daily.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. Increase the soda dispenser nozzle cleaning frequency to daily, as the manufacturer recommends. The EHS discussed this with the PIC and the food employee.

out_items.name: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding

violations.title: Reheating for Hot Holding, Proper Temp
violations.observation: The following food item(s) was not reheated for hot holding to a sufficient temperature and/or time: black beans, BBQ pork, chili were not reheated properly and on placed on the steam table.
violations.corrective_action: All reheated food placed on the steam table must be reheated to 165ºF for at least 15 seconds before being placed on the steam table. The PIC had the products reheated in the microwave to the proper temperature and time.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: black beans on the steam table were 115º, BBQ pork was 78º, chili was 133º and 93º. Hot dogs were 125º and 122º.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. All foods were reheated to 165º for 15 seconds in the microwave or the oven.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. Bottles of hand sanitizer and cough medicine were stored with food products on a shelf above the food prep table. This violation was also cited on the last routine inspection.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. Store chemicals separate from and not above food prep and storage areas. The PIC corrected this during the inspection by moving the chemicals. PARK AVENUE CAFE (Inspection Date: 06/17/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints. One of the food handlers was not wearing a hair restraints while preparing sandwiches on the prep line. This violation was also cited on the last routine inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. Have all food handlers wear a proper hair restraints while working with foods. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter. There was a sanitizer bucket for wet wiping cloths to be stored in, but there were several wiping cloths on the food prep counter that were not stored in it.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. Ensure staff store wet wiping cloths in the sanitizer solution between uses, not the counter. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Surfaces of ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment are not being cleaned as required. There is some visible soil on the white part inside the ice machine. The back side of the slicer (under the tray where foods area placed) was also in need of cleaning.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. Please clean this area. While cleaning, prevent contaminating the ice. Clean the soiled part of the slicer.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: Time as a Public Health Control, Written Procedures
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide written procedures for the use of time as a public health control with the following time/temperature control for safety food item(s): items on the salad bar were being stored with TPHC, but there was no agreement or procedures in the record.
violations.corrective_action: If time only is used as a public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety food before cooking or for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that is displayed or held for service for immediate consumption, written procedures shall be prepared in advance and maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request. The EHS provided the person in charge with a TPHC document and procedures for all items on the salad bar, which will be followed.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Storage-Personal Care Items
violations.observation: Observed personal care items such as NyQuil and hand sanitizer stored on a shelf with foods such as peanut butter, cooking spray, and condiments.
violations.corrective_action: All employees' personal care items shall be stored in a way that prevents the contamination of food and food contact surfaces through improper labeling or storage. Separate the personal care items from the foods as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: a covered 6-inch stainless steel container of cooked pasteurized eggs was full of cooked eggs and 125ºF in the walk-in for about 1 hour.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. The food employee removed the eggs from the walk-in, uncovered them, and placed them on an ice bath to cool. Cool to 70º within 1 hour, or discard the eggs.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. In the walk-in a stainless steel pan of packaged melon was stored on the floor.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. Do not store foods on the floor. PARK AVENUE CAFE (Inspection Date: 12/19/2025) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints. Two food employees were observed preparing food without wearing hair restraints.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. Correct as soon as possible or within 6 months.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed the following areas were in need of cleaning due to food debris and build-up: - the floor behind and under the main prep top refrigerator -the wall behind the food prep area where the can opener is located
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. Please clean these areas as soon as possible or within 6 months.

violations.title: Mops Allowed to Air Dry
violations.observation: Observed that mops are improperly stored between use and in the basin of the mop sink.
violations.corrective_action: Store mops in a position that allows them to air dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies, such as on the provided mop rack.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 70F, No More than 2 Hours
violations.observation: OBSERVATION: Cooked chicken placed on a tray on the counter top for cooling registered a temperature between 100-110F,discussion with CFM showed it had been prepared 2 hours ago. The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours.Chicken
violations.corrective_action: CORRECTION: The Chicken was discarded. Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: OBSERVATION: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: Items in the salad bar.
violations.corrective_action: CORRECTION: Discussed with the manager, who marked time from 10:30 AM-2:30 PM. If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to-eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: CHILI (87F), WHITE RICE (123F), MEATBALL (128F), AND MARINARA SAUCE (118) WERE STOED ON STEAM TABLE FOR ABOUT 30 MINUTES.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. CFM REHEATED CHILI TO 184F, WHITE RICE TO 174F, MEATBALL TO 172F, AND MARINARA SAUCE TO 175F.
